exposure: Obstetric unit closures (leading to physician relocation)
Changes in hospital-level norms for obstetric clinical decision-making
outcome: Physicians' treatment decisions for newborn deliveries
Delivering newborns without any procedure behavior change
cohort: The study examined hospital-based births in Florida from 2003 through 2017, focusing on births attributed to physicians continuously observed 2 years before and 2 years after an obstetric unit closure (treatment group) or around a placebo closure date (control group).
finding: Obstetric physicians sharply became less aggressive in their newborn birth clinical management (e.g., use of C-section) after relocating to new hospitals with more conservative practices, demonstrating high malleability to practice patterns of other physicians.
mod_finding: Treatment group physicians showed an immediate 11-percentage point (33%) increase in delivering newborns without any procedure, indicating a sharp decrease in C-section use and other interventions.
